# specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md

```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

**Source:** outcomes O1–O3, as agreed with the human partner on 2026-11-06 and
ranked in the order they gave. One track, a known progression.
**Background, not a driving spec:**
[sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md](sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md)
(PROPOSED, 2026-10-05) and
[sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md](sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md)
(Proposed, 2026-10-05).
**Repository state at derivation:** one commit, "initial commit". There are four
`uv init` package scaffolds and no tests.

## Gap analysis

| Req | Verdict | Evidence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 Index files → one filing-index table | missing | none found. Each `packages/*/src/*/__init__.py` holds only the `hello()` stub, and each package declares `dependencies = []` | The background spec covers this outcome (§§2.1, 4.2–4.6, 6) but is unaccepted (§7 step 1). Its Azure platform (R4, ADR) is background, not a commitment. |
| O2 Submissions named by index rows, downloaded | missing | none found (same scaffolds) | Background spec §2.2 lists this out of scope. The partner moved it into this roadmap on 2026-11-06. |
| O3 10-K and 8-K handled: selected, main documents extracted | missing | none found (same scaffolds) | Background spec §2.2 lists filing-text extraction out of scope. Brought into scope as for O2. |
| — Root script `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` | in-code-but-not-in-spec | `pyproject.toml` (root) | No `sec_edgar` module exists. Each stage should either adopt or remove it. |
| — Four packages (`client`, `download`, `index-ingest`, `ingest`) | in-code-but-not-in-spec | `packages/` | Background spec §4.9 proposes a single `sec-edgar-ingest` package. Stage 1 decides how work maps onto packages. |

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index ingestion
      Objective: Ingest the quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table.
      Spec: O1; background spec §§2.1, 3 (R5, R6, R8–R10), 4.2–4.6, 5, 6 — adopt or amend at brainstorming
      Gap closed: O1; root-script and package-layout rows (first decision)
      Consumes: package scaffolds only
      Produces: a filing-index table with archive path and CIK per row; a shared, throttled SEC downloader with an identifying User-Agent; a recorded package layout
      Exit: From committed quarterly and daily fixtures, CI builds the table with no duplicate logical rows on re-run. A bounded live smoke test of one archived quarter plus one daily index records row count and request rate.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the individual submissions that the index rows name.
      Spec: O2 (no stage spec yet; background spec §2.2 excludes it)
      Gap closed: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table and shared downloader
      Produces: retained submission files, addressable from their index row; a measured per-submission byte count and download rate
      Exit: For a bounded sample of index rows, every named submission is stored or reported as pending or failed. A re-run issues no SEC requests for submissions already stored. The measured cost replaces O2's estimate in this roadmap.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Select the 10-K and 8-K filings from the stored submissions and extract each one's main document.
      Spec: O3 (no stage spec yet; background spec §2.2 excludes text extraction)
      Gap closed: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's stored submissions and measured cost
      Produces: the 10-K and 8-K main documents, linked to their index rows
      Exit: From committed submission fixtures, CI selects every 10-K and 8-K, amendments included, and extracts one main document per filing. A filing with an unrecognized structure is reported, not dropped.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

Order follows the partner's ranking, which here is also the dependency order.
Each stage consumes the previous stage's output: O2 reads the paths that O1's
rows name, and O3 reads the files that O2 stores.

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O3 and the
in-code-but-not-in-spec rows against the accumulated system. Each verdict gets
evidence: the implementing stage plan, its Deviation notes and any
`specs/deferred_items.md` entries. An unmet row either becomes a new stage or
is deferred with a written reason. Only then does the roadmap retire to
`specs/completed/`.
```
